figures.finding: Norfolk Island has no screen agreement of its own: from 1 July 2016 the Fair Work Act 2009 counts Norfolk Island as part of Australia, and Commonwealth Acts and New South Wales laws are the laws in force there, so an actor's terms there are Australia's.

value.basis: Fair Work Act 2009 s12 definition of Australia (inserted by the Territories Legislation Amendment Act 2016, Sch 5 item 51); Norfolk Island Act 1979 ss15, 18A (inserted by the Norfolk Island Legislation Amendment Act 2015)

figures.applies: Norfolk Island (external territory of Australia), from 1 July 2016.

sources.said: Fair Work Act 2009 51 Section 12 Insert: Australia means the Commonwealth of Australia and, when used in a geographical sense, includes Norfolk Island, the Territory of Christmas Island and the Territory of Cocos (Keeling) Islands, but does not include any other external Territory.

15 Laws in force in the Territory After the final transition time, the laws in force in the Territory from time to time are: (a) Acts to the extent that they are in force from time to time in, or in relation to, the Territory; … 18A Application of New South Wales laws (1) Subject to this section and section 18B, the provisions of the law of New South Wales (whether made before or after the final transition time), as in force in New South Wales from time to time, are in force in the Territory.
